title: Customized, production ready inference with open source models: Dmytro (Dima) Dzhulgakov

primary.label: Inference & Model Systems
primary.rationale: Selected by Jev (System One, jev-1.13.0) from the 17-category taxonomy using the talk's summary, takeaways, concepts and technologies (confidence 96%).

domains.label: General Purpose
domains.rationale: The talk centers on Fireworks' custom serving stack built from CUDA kernels, LoRA-based multi-model deployment, serverless inference pricing, and latency-throughput optimization for production LLM serving. Fireworks is an inference platform that other software teams build on to deploy and serve AI models. The talk covers prototyping via serverless pay-per-token tier and production deployment at enterprise scale with dedicated hardware. Content assumes familiarity with LLM inference, GPU optimization, fine-tuning, and production ML deployment. Live conference presentation at AI Engineer World's Fair with an integrated product demo. All evidence anchors are direct excerpts from the transcript with grade said_in_transcript.

summary: Dmytro Dzhulgakov, co-founder and CTO of Fireworks AI and a PyTorch core maintainer for five years, presents on productionizing open source AI models. The founding team combines PyTorch leadership experience from Meta and Google AI. He argues that while proprietary models like GPT-4 remain dominant in production, open source models are gaining share due to three advantages: lower latency (especially critical for real-time and agentic use cases), dramatically lower cost, and domain adaptability through fine-tuning. He quantifies the cost gap — GPT-4 with 5K-token prompts across 10K users making 20 daily calls can cost ~$10K/day or ~$7M/year, whereas smaller fine-tuned models like Llama 3 can match quality at 10x speed improvement. However, open models face three challenges: complicated setup and maintenance (GPU sourcing, framework selection, model optimization), non-trivial multi-attribute optimization (latency vs throughput, prompt length), and production readiness (GPU reliability, scalability, telemetry). Fireworks addresses these with a ground-up custom serving stack including custom CUDA kernels, benchmarked as fastest for long-prompt LLM inference and image generation (SDXL, SD3). The platform supports Llama, Gemma, ASR/TTS models, and partner models. LoRA-based deployment enables thousands of fine-tuned model variants on a single GPU with serverless pay-per-token pricing. Dzhulgakov then covers compound AI systems, where models combine with RAG, function calling, and external tools. He demonstrates FireFunction V, an open source function-calling model combining free-form chat with tool use — stock queries, chart plotting, image generation — requiring complex multi-step reasoning and contextual awareness. The demo app is open source on GitHub. Fireworks offers tiered product offerings from serverless inference (pay-per-token) through on-demand dedicated hardware to enterprise-scale with personalized hardware tuning. The platform is OpenAI API compatible, supporting frameworks like LangChain and LlamaIndex. Production customers include Quora (Poe), Cursor, Sourcegraph, Upstage, and Liner, with Fireworks serving over 150 billion tokens per day. External data from LangChain's state of AI shows Fireworks as one of the most popular model-pulling platforms after HuggingFace.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: Introduction and Background
sections.summary: Dima introduces himself as co-founder/CTO of Fireworks AI, substituting for co-founder Lino. The founding team comes from PyTorch leads at Meta and Google AI veterans with a decade of productionizing AI experience. Dima has been a PyTorch core maintainer for 5 years, motivating their belief in open source models.

sections.title: Why Open Source Models Are Growing
sections.summary: Proprietary models like GPT-4 are good but serve all use cases the same way, causing high latency and unnecessary cost for narrow domains. Smaller fine-tuned models (Llama, Gemma) can match quality at 10x speed. Cost example: GPT-4 with 5K-token prompts across 10K users costs ~$7M/year. Open models excel at domain adaptability with thousands of fine-tuned variants available.

sections.title: Challenges with Open Models
sections.summary: Three challenges: complicated setup/maintenance (GPU sourcing, frameworks, model optimization repeated on every update), non-trivial multi-attribute optimization (latency vs throughput, prompt length), and production readiness (GPU reliability, scalability, telemetry, observability).

sections.title: Fireworks Custom Serving Stack and Optimization
sections.summary: Fireworks built a ground-up custom serving stack from CUDA kernels to orchestration, benchmarked as fastest for long-prompt LLM inference and image generation (SDXL, SD3). Supports Llama, Gemma, ASR/TTS, and partner models. Offers fine-tuning platform and LoRA-based deployment of thousands of model variants on a single GPU with serverless pay-per-token pricing.

sections.title: Compound AI Systems and Function Calling
sections.summary: Models alone are not products — compound AI systems combine RAG, function calling, external tools, and domain-specialized models. Function calling sits at the core of emerging agentic architecture, connecting LLMs to external APIs. Fireworks focuses on function-specialized models for this paradigm.

sections.title: FireFunction Demo and Contextual Awareness
sections.summary: Dima demos FireFunction V (released two weeks prior), an open source model combining free-form chat with function calling. The demo app queries stock quotes for top three cloud providers (AWS/GCP/Azure), plots bar charts, and generates images — requiring multi-step reasoning to translate user queries into sequential function calls. Contextual awareness maintains prior context across turns (e.g., adding Oracle to existing graph) and drops it when topics change. The demo is open source on GitHub, built with FireFunction and SDXL, using structured generation with JSON grammar mode.

sections.title: Product Offerings and Getting Started
sections.summary: Fireworks offers tiered products progressing from prototyping to enterprise: serverless inference (pay-per-token, no hardware configuration), on-demand (dedicated hardware with customization), and enterprise scale (discounted long-term contracts with personalized hardware setup and performance tuning). Fine-tuning can be hosted on-platform or users can bring their own LoRA adapters. The platform is OpenAI API compatible, supporting tools like LangChain and LlamaIndex.

sections.title: Production Customers and Scale
sections.summary: Fireworks serves over 150 billion tokens per day for production customers ranging from startups to enterprises, including Quora (Poe chatbots), Cursor (code assistant with latency-critical requirements), Sourcegraph, Upstage, and Liner. External LangChain state-of-AI data ranks Fireworks among the most popular platforms for pulling models after HuggingFace. Dima invites developers to try the playground and visit Fireworks at the Expo booth.
